text: Git is a popular version control system that helps developers track changes in their code. One of its most useful features is branching, which allows you to work on different tasks without affecting the main code. A common practice is to create feature branches for new work, so the main branch stays safe and stable. When your work is finished, you can merge your branch back into the main one. Many teams also use pull requests to review changes before merging, which improves code quality. This branching workflow makes teamwork easier and keeps projects organised.
